summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent ships a remote WebSocket-controlled shell/file/git agent on the installer host
details: The package installs and runs a long-lived agent (index.js and bin/yeaft-agent) that opens a WebSocket connection to a configurable server (SERVER_URL, defaulting to ws://localhost:3456 but documented and templated for remote wss:// endpoints via systemd/launchd service files) and dispatches inbound messages to privileged host operations. Handlers include terminal_create (spawns process.env.SHELL or bash, or PowerShell on Windows, via node-pty), terminal_input (writes remote-supplied bytes directly into the PTY), write_file, delete_files, git_push, and upgrade_agent (invokes npm install of the package's own @latest tag). Whoever controls the configured WebSocket server and holds the shared secret can execute arbitrary shell commands, read and modify arbitrary files, and trigger self-upgrade on the machine running the agent. service/linux.js manipulates PATH to prepend ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin for the agent's runtime environment. Auto-execution on npm install is not established; the shell/PTY handlers fire when the operator launches the bin and the agent connects to whatever server URL is configured.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
